questions.q: What was missing from this course's earlier bronze.trips naming?
options: The catalog part — the real, full name under Unity Catalog is catalog.schema.table, like nyc_taxi.bronze.trips
Nothing was missing; bronze.trips was always the complete name
The table name itself was always incomplete
It was missing a metastore-region prefix
questions.explain: The schema.table naming was valid, but implicitly relied on whatever catalog was already the current default.

questions.q: What do USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA do?
options: Set a session's current default catalog/schema, letting shorter names resolve unambiguously without typing the full three-part name every time
Permanently rename a catalog or schema
Grant permissions on a catalog to a user
Delete an existing catalog or schema
questions.explain: This is exactly the shorthand earlier lessons were implicitly relying on, made explicit here.

questions.q: Why can dev.bronze.trips and prod.bronze.trips coexist as completely separate tables?
options: The catalog is part of a table's identity — two tables with the same schema.table name in different catalogs are genuinely different tables
They're actually the same table, just accessed two different ways
Unity Catalog doesn't allow the same schema.table name to exist in two catalogs
One of them must always be a view, not a real table
questions.explain: This is a real, common pattern — develop against dev, run the same code against prod.

questions.q: How does spark.table("trips") (Lesson 16) resolve under Unity Catalog's three-level namespace?
options: It resolves using the session's current catalog and schema, set via USE CATALOG/USE SCHEMA
It always resolves to a fixed, hardcoded catalog regardless of session context
It fails immediately unless the full three-part name is given
It ignores Unity Catalog entirely and reads directly from DBFS
questions.explain: This connects the shorthand table access from earlier lessons to the real namespace resolution happening underneath.

questions.q: What's the benefit of developing against dev.bronze.trips and later running the same code against prod.bronze.trips?
options: The exact same code runs against either environment, just by changing which catalog is current
It requires rewriting all table references for each environment
It only works if dev and prod share the exact same metastore region
There's no real benefit; it's purely a naming convention with no practical use
questions.explain: This is a real, common pattern enabled directly by the catalog being part of a table's identity.
